arxiv-1509-08896.title: Quadratic polynomials of small modulus cannot represent OR
arxiv-1509-08896.creator: Holden Lee
arxiv-1509-08896.description: Abstract An open problem in complexity theory is to find the minimal degree of a polynomial representing the n n -bit OR function modulo composite m m . This problem is related to understanding the power of circuits with MOD m \text{MOD}_{m} gates where m m is composite.

arxiv-2012-09424.title: Predicting Events in MOBA Games: Prediction, Attribution, and Evaluation
arxiv-2012-09424.creator: Zelong Yang, Yan Wang, Piji Li, Shaobin Lin, Shuming Shi, Shao-Lun Huang, and Wei Bi
arxiv-2012-09424.description: Abstract The multiplayer online battle arena (MOBA) games have become increasingly popular in recent years. Consequently, many efforts have been devoted to providing pre-game or in-game predictions for them. These predictions can be used in many MOBA esports related applications, such as AI commentator systems, in-game data analysis, and game-assistant bots.

arxiv-2109-11477.title: Synthesis of Partially Observed Jump-Diffusion Systems via Control Barrier Functions
arxiv-2109-11477.creator: Niloofar Jahanshahi 1∗†, Pushpak Jagtap 2∗†, Majid Zamani 3,1
arxiv-2109-11477.description: Abstract . In this paper, we study formal synthesis of control policies for partially observed jump-diffusion systems against complex logic specifications. Given a state estimator, we utilize a discretization-free approach for formal synthesis of control policies by using a notation of control barrier functions without requiring any knowledge of the estimation accuracy.

arxiv-2212-10442.title: Link auxiliary field method in the Extended Hubbard model
arxiv-2212-10442.creator: Sergey Mostovoy, Oleg Pavlovsky
arxiv-2212-10442.description: Abstract The aim of this work is to generalize the method of Hubbard fields in fermion Quantum Monte Carlo simulation to the case of link fields. The introduced Hubbard link fields play a role of the interaction fields responsible for the attraction and repulsion of electronic excitations at the nodes.

arxiv-2401-02681.title: Displaying risk in mergers: a diagrammatic approach for exchange ratio determination
arxiv-2401-02681.creator: Alessandra Mainini, Enrico Moretto ∗,, Daniela Visetti
arxiv-2401-02681.description: Abstract This article extends, in a stochastic setting, previous results in the determination of feasible exchange ratios for merging companies. A first outcome is that shareholders of the companies involved in the merging process face both an upper and a lower bounds for acceptable exchange ratios.

arxiv-2404-15213.title: Automatic Classification of Subjective Time Perception Using Multi-modal Physiological Data of Air Traffic Controllers
arxiv-2404-15213.creator: Till Aust, Eirini Balta, Argiro Vatakis, Heiko Hamann
arxiv-2404-15213.description: Abstract In high-pressure environments where human individuals must simultaneously monitor multiple entities, communicate effectively, and maintain intense focus, the perception of time becomes a critical factor influencing performance and well-being. One indicator of well-being can be the person’s subjective time perception. In our project ChronoPilot , we aim to develop a device that modulates human subjective time perception.

arxiv-2503-03472.title: Interaction-correlated random matrices
arxiv-2503-03472.creator: Abbas Ali Saberi, Sina Saber, Roderich Moessner
arxiv-2503-03472.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Abbas Ali Saberi, Sina Saber, Roderich Moessner. We introduce a family of random matrices where correlations between matrix elements are induced via interaction-derived Boltzmann factors. Varying these yields access to different ensembles. We find a universal scaling behavior of the finite-size statistics characterized by a heavy-tailed eigenvalue distribution whose extremes are governed by the Fréchet extreme value distribution for the case corresponding to a ferromagnetic Ising transition. The introduction of a finite density of nonlocal interactions restores standard random matrix behavior.

arxiv-2503-14450.title: Approximation of diffeomorphisms for quantum state transfers
arxiv-2503-14450.creator: Eugenio Pozzoli 1, Alessandro Scagliotti 2,3
arxiv-2503-14450.description: Abstract . In this paper, we seek to combine two emerging standpoints in control theory. On the one hand, recent advances in infinite-dimensional geometric control have unlocked a method for controlling (with arbitrary precision and in arbitrarily small times) state transfers for bilinear Schrödinger PDEs posed on a Riemannian manifold M M .

pmc-10505167.title: Blocking insulin-like growth factor 1 receptor signaling pathway inhibits neuromuscular junction regeneration after botulinum toxin-A treatment
pmc-10505167.creator: Hiroki Ishihara, Yoshinori Otani, Kazuki Tanaka, Hisao Miyajima, Huy Xuan Ngo, Masashi Fujitani
pmc-10505167.description: Botulinum toxin-A (BTX) administration into muscle is an established treatment for conditions with excessive muscle contraction. However, botulinum therapy has short-term effectiveness, and high-dose injection of BTX could induce neutralizing antibodies against BTX. Therefore, prolonging its effects could be beneficial in a clinical situation.

pmc-10614450.title: Hypothalamic-Pituitary Axis Function and Adrenal Insufficiency in COVID-19 Patients
pmc-10614450.creator: Emre Durcan, Aysa Hacioglu, Zuleyha Karaca, Kursad Unluhizarci, Mustafa Sait Gonen, Fahrettin Kelestimur
pmc-10614450.description: The outbreak of COVID-19 has affected more than half a billion people worldwide and caused more than 6 million deaths since 2019. The responsible virus, severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), primarily affects the lungs, but it has multisystemic effects. It is well known that dysfunction of multiple endocrine organs may occur during or after COVID-19.

pmc-10735979.title: RACISM IN RESEARCH ON OLDER MIGRANTS AND ETHNO-RACIAL MINORITIES: INSIGHTS FROM TWO SCOPING REVIEWS
pmc-10735979.creator: Sandra Torres
pmc-10735979.description: The study of ethno-racialized minorities used to be primarily the domain of American social gerontologists. Meta-analyses of this scholarship have shown that this research has so far been characterized by two sets of practices: it engages in racialization but vaguely acknowledges racism, and it seems inequality-obsessed but justice-oblivious.

pmc-11053346.title: The genome sequence of a leaf beetle, Cryptocephalus moraei (Linnaeus, 1758)
pmc-11053346.creator: Olga Sivell, Duncan Sivell, Ryan Mitchell, Natural History Museum Genome Acquisition Lab, Darwin Tree of Life Barcoding collective, Wellcome Sanger Institute Tree of Life programme, Wellcome Sanger Institute Scientific Operations: DNA Pipelines collective, Tree of Life Core Informatics collective, D
pmc-11053346.description: We present a genome assembly from an individual female Cryptocephalus moraei (a leaf beetle; Arthropoda; Insecta; Coleoptera; Chrysomelidae). The genome sequence is 500.5 megabases in span. Most of the assembly is scaffolded into 15 chromosomal pseudomolecules, including the X sex chromosome. The mitochondrial genome has also been assembled and is 15.68 kilobases in length.

pmc-12533933.title: Predicting Risk of Heat-Related Injuries for Individuals Wearing Personal Protective Equipment Using Smartwatches: Feasibility Observational Study
pmc-12533933.creator: Meghan Hegarty-Craver, Donna Womack, Jonathan Thornburg, Timothy Boe, M John Archer, Worth Calfee, Amaryllis Mavragani
pmc-12533933.description: BackgroundThe risk of developing heat-related illness increases when personal protective equipment (PPE) is worn, especially in hot and humid environments. While cooling strategies are effective, they must be applied preemptively or delivered promptly, which can be difficult if individuals are working in dangerous environments or wearing contaminated PPE.

pmc-12951520.title: Dynamic crotonylation of Bub3 regulates mitotic checkpoint silencing and chromosome segregation
pmc-12951520.creator: Xufan Shi, Xingchen Yu, Wenwen Wang, Fangyuan Xiong, Xiao Yuan, Qing Hu, Xiaoyu Song, Zhen Dou, Xuebiao Yao, Liangyu Zhang
pmc-12951520.description: nce mechanism that senses the faulty kinetochore–microtubule attachment and catalyzes the assembly of the mitotic checkpoint complex (MCC). The MCC prevents the transition from metaphase to anaphase by inhibiting the E3 ligase activity of anaphase-promoting complex/cyclosome (APC/C) until all chromosomes are properly bi-oriented with spindle microtubules from the opposite poles.

pmc-13069099.title: The structure and function of taste G protein-coupled receptors and their implications in diseases
pmc-13069099.creator: Ruohan Zhai, Xihao Yong, Peihua Jiang, Marco Tizzano, Zhenhua Shao, Wei Yan, Xin Zheng
pmc-13069099.description: Taste G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), including sweet (TAS1Rs) and bitter (TAS2Rs) taste receptors, are essential for detecting nutrients and avoiding toxins, influencing dietary behavior, metabolism, and overall health. Beyond their role in taste perception, these receptors are widely expressed in extra-gustatory tissues, including the respiratory and gastrointestinal systems, where they regulate innate immune responses, hormone secretion, and energy balance.

pmc-13385650.title: C2orf74 orchestrates germ-Leydig crosstalk to inhibit white adipose tissue browning in male mice
pmc-13385650.creator: Li Zhao, Jialuo Han, Xinxin Wang, Qin Li, Qinghua Shi, Fangbiao Tao, Pilong Li, Chengxin Zhang, Qiang Liu, Juan Zhang
pmc-13385650.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Sex differences in obesity are well recognized; however, the identification of sex-specific obesity genes and the mechanisms through which they affect obesity development remain elusive. Here, we identify a germ-cell-specific gene C2orf74, whose expression is responsive to high-fat diet (HFD) and promotes HFD-induced obesity in male mice by restraining lipolysis and limiting the browning of white adipocytes through suppression of androgen receptor signaling, but not in females.

pmc-13394076.title: Epileptic drop attacks: More than just atonic seizures
pmc-13394076.creator: Tomonori Ono, Kazuaki Sato, Ryoko Honda, Hiroshi Otsubo
pmc-13394076.description: “Drop attacks” are not officially defined by the International League Against Epilepsy. Seizures are characterized by a sudden loss of control over the trunk and posture, leading to falls and injuries, and resolving within a few seconds. Accurately diagnosing the type of seizure is usually difficult due to limitations in clinical documentation based on witness or physician inspections.

pmc-13656042.title: Building a bridge over troubled waters during salvage esophageal reconstruction
pmc-13656042.creator: Ian G. Christie, Evan T. Alicuben, Ryan M. Levy
pmc-13656042.description: ng the patient undue morbidity, often via alternative anatomic routes. Barron and colleagues report an impressive 25-year experience with salvage esophageal reconstruction using colonic interposition, in which microvascular augmentation was associated with a marked reduction in anastomotic leak (1).
